e: The application is reached at the transport layer (layer 4), so a Network Load Balancer fits, and an Auto Scaling group spanning multiple Availability Zones with health checks replaces failed instances and spreads capacity, giving high availability cost-effectively. Adding an ALB too, Route 53-only routing, or restart alarms is less effective or costs more.

API Gateway with Lambda serves the dynamic form and handles submissions, and a second Lambda publishing to an SNS topic emails the company, all pay-per-use, which is cheapest for under 100 visits a month. ECS, EC2 with IIS, or Amplify with SQS cost more or can't send email.

Each account's root user should have its own unique, company-managed distribution-list email (root emails must be unique per account), and alternate contacts for billing, operations, and security point to the right team distribution lists. Individual mailboxes or a single shared address for all accounts are less secure or not allowed.

An SQS queue decouples purchases from processing so peak load is buffered and workers scale on queue depth rather than timing out, and an ElastiCache layer in front of Aurora offloads repeated reads, reducing database load at low cost. Retries on Lambda or EC2 and API usage plans don't fix the peak capacity problem.

QuickSight dashboards can query the Cost and Usage Report data in S3 through Athena (using the CUR's Athena integration), enabling a daily NAT gateway cost table that is shared with leadership. DataSync doesn't query data, and CloudWatch dashboards aren't built for CUR analysis.

Setting a short default TTL (2 minutes) on CloudFront limits how long stale content is cached, and long max-age caching combined with an invalidation on each deployment gives strong caching while clearing changed files from edge caches immediately. S3 has no default TTL setting, and a private directive prevents shared caching.

A Compute Savings Plan applies to EC2 and also to Lambda usage, so it covers the growing number of Lambda functions, and connecting the Lambda functions to the private subnets gives them direct network access to the EC2 instances. EC2 Instance Savings Plans don't cover Lambda, and public subnets or the Lambda service VPC wouldn't reach private instances.

AWS Budgets per developer account with alerts and Budgets actions that apply a deny policy when the budget is reached actively limits spending with little overhead. Cost Explorer, anomaly detection, tagging, or scheduled stops only report or are laborious.

Least-privilege security groups chain tiers by referencing security groups: the web tier accepts HTTPS from the ALB's group, the application tier accepts HTTPS from the web tier's group, and the database tier accepts SQL Server traffic from the application tier's group. Broad outbound rules or database-to-web rules aren't needed.

A Compute Savings Plan covers EC2, Fargate, and Lambda, and a SageMaker Savings Plan covers SageMaker, so two plans cover all four services. EC2 Instance Savings Plans don't cover Fargate, Lambda, or SageMaker, and Compute Savings Plans don't cover SageMaker.

Use SCT and DMS to convert the schema and migrate the data to Aurora PostgreSQL, and enable Babelfish for Aurora PostgreSQL so the applications can keep sending T-SQL queries over the SQL Server wire protocol, minimizing code changes. SCT and DMS don't rewrite application queries, and RDS Proxy is just pooling.

Turning on EC2 'EBS encryption by default' for the account and Region encrypts every newly created volume and snapshot copy and prevents creating unencrypted volumes. AWS Config only detects noncompliance, and Systems Manager or Migration Hub don't enforce default encryption.

Kinesis Data Streams in on-demand mode scales automatically with fluctuating clickstream traffic, and Lambda can process the records in real time. Firehose is near-real-time delivery, Video Streams is for video, and Flink doesn't ingest data by itself.

S3 Storage Lens gives organization-wide, cross-Region visibility into bucket configuration, including which buckets don't have versioning enabled. CloudTrail, Access Analyzer, and Multi-Region Access Points don't report on versioning status.

After 30 days the files are rarely accessed but must be immediately accessible and can't be recreated, so S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval (lowest-cost storage with millisecond access, multi-AZ resilience) is the cheapest fit, with deletion after 4 years. One Zone-IA risks data loss, and Standard-IA costs more, while Glacier Flexible Retrieval isn't immediate.

An S3 Multi-Region Access Point provides a single global endpoint that routes requests over the AWS global network to the nearest bucket and fails over automatically, with Cross-Region Replication keeping buckets in sync in an active-active setup, with little management. Regional endpoints require client-side failover logic.

An Auto Scaling group with min and max of one, launched from an AMI, automatically replaces a failed instance (and can recover in another AZ) without any application change, and an ALB provides a stable endpoint. Running two copies may not work for legacy applications that can't be changed, backups are slow to restore, and refactoring isn't allowed.

AWS Control Tower creates accounts with automatic guardrails, and a central networking account that shares VPC subnets with workload accounts through AWS RAM centrally manages the networking with the least overhead. Plain Organizations lacks guardrails, and per-account VPCs with inspection VPCs add management.

Hosting static content in S3 behind CloudFront is the cheapest, highly scalable design that removes the EC2 instances and ALB. ElastiCache doesn't front S3, and Amplify with an ALB or EC2 caches keep unneeded compute costs.

Amazon FSx for Windows File Server is a fully managed SMB file system, requiring the least administration for SMB access. Volume or tape gateways are block or tape interfaces, and a Windows EC2 file server must be managed.

An Aurora global database replicates to the secondary Region with typically under one second of lag (meeting the 5-minute RPO) and supports managed failover within minutes (meeting the 20-minute RTO), with minimal configuration changes. Cross-Region read replicas, new clusters, or DMS take more setup and are slower to recover.

A Fargate task started by EventBridge Scheduler can run a stateful job for over an hour without being interrupted and needs no servers. Lambda is limited to 15 minutes, Spot Instances can be interrupted, and DataSync doesn't run jobs.

Amazon Security Lake automatically centralizes security data from AWS services, third-party sources, and multiple accounts into a purpose-built data lake in S3 using the OCSF format, with the least development effort. Lake Formation, Lambda, or DMS approaches require building the pipelines.

A transit gateway connects many VPCs in a hub-and-spoke model with route tables controlling reachability, so shared services and application-to-application communication scale to 100+ VPCs with the least administration. Peering and VPN meshes become unmanageable, and Direct Connect isn't for VPC-to-VPC links.

ECS Anywhere runs ECS tasks on the company's on-premises servers (external launch type) in the same cluster as Fargate tasks in the cloud, giving a single container platform, and an Application Load Balancer handles the HTTP traffic for the cloud services. Fargate can't run on premises, and an NLB is for layer 4.
